description.value:
Task Type: Design Project (Folio + VR Prototype + Pitch)
Scenario: Students are commissioned to redesign a specific, constrained interior space (e.g., a sustainable micro-apartment, an accessible teenage retreat, or a modern collaborative workspace) for a distinct client persona.

Part 1: The Design Folio (Investigating & Generating)

Needs Analysis: Students critique the client’s brief, investigating the functional, aesthetic, and spatial constraints of the room.

Ideation: Development of mood boards, 2D floor plans, and color/material palettes.

Tech Integration: Documenting how VR tools will be used to test and refine the scale and flow of the design.

Part 2: The Immersive Prototype (Producing)

Virtual Construction: Using Home Design 3D VR/VisualizeR on the Meta Quest 3S to build out the designed space.

Iterative Testing: Students must document at least two significant changes made to their design after experiencing it in VR (e.g., realizing a kitchen island restricts traffic flow when viewed at a 1:1 scale).

Part 3: The Client Walkthrough (Evaluating)

Presentation: A live or recorded walkthrough of the virtual space.

Justification: Students evaluate their final solution against their initial success criteria, explaining how their design choices meet the client's needs and how VR testing improved the final outcome.

context.value:
In this 10-week unit, students investigate the intersection of interior architecture and digital technology within the materials, technologies, and built environments context. They examine how human-centred design, ergonomics, and aesthetic principles influence spatial interactions, while evaluating the lifecycle and sustainability of contemporary materials to design for preferred futures. Moving beyond conventional two-dimensional floor plans, students utilise immersive virtual reality (VR) technologies to analyse architectural scale, volumetric proportion, and spatial flow.

Applying iterative design thinking and project management skills, students develop and prototype an interior environment in response to a simulated client brief. Using specialised 3D modelling and visualisation software, students generate, refine, and render dynamic spatial concepts. The unit culminates in a digital presentation and 1:1 scale virtual walkthrough, where students communicate their design processes, defend material and layout decisions, and evaluate their designed solution against functional, social, and environmental success criteria.
